headline: Every bottle checked, not a sample.
formProduct: Wine in 750 mL bottles, own brands
label: #F7F2E6
heroLede: At 36,000 bottles an hour, one wrong label or crooked cap becomes thousands of bottles before anyone sees it. Here's what a camera check could look like on your bottling line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bottle has its closure on, straight and fully seated. A crooked screw cap lets air in, and the wine is spoiled by the time someone opens it.
labelLede: A shiraz and a merlot go into the same bottle and look much the same at line speed, and export markets each need their own label. The camera checks every bottle carries the right label for the run, straight and intact.
codeLede: The lot code ties every bottle back to its tank and vintage. The system reads the printed code on every bottle and compares it with the wine and lot set at changeover.
objectLede: Glass fragments, capsule offcuts and loose parts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four crooked closures in fifteen minutes. Check the closer.
